preamble: Loss of implosion in the velar implosive: [ɠ] becomes plain [g]. Ehret (1991) reconstructs a Proto-Eastern Cushitic velar implosive *gʼ (= ɠ) alongside *g, mainly because Dullay and Yaaku keep them apart: *g devoiced there to k, while *gʼ stayed voiced and is still implosive in Yaaku and some Dullay varieties such as Gollango and Saamakko. In Lowland and Highland East Cushitic (Afar, Somali, Oromo, Sidamo, Burji) *gʼ merged with *g. Sasse (1979) does not reconstruct *gʼ, so the starting point is Ehret's reconstruction and is disputed.
